suggestions.title: 1. Chest Pain: mild or serious, and what to do with each
suggestions.reading: The whole section in the first batch: [AI Detected, 78%](https://www.pangram.com/history/ce00d5dc-1e58-4c03-9b82-628409d40764), this paragraph in its AI High window.
suggestions.tested:
Written against your fixes, read by a fresh reader with the eight differences after each of three drafts and changed every time: "For chest pain that's mild and familiar, I'd just use DMSO, as long as it's holding steady and they're fully alert. It's more serious if: ... Hard movement brought it on, like dancing or climbing stairs. ... When you're unsure which kind it is, treat it as the serious kind.": [AI Generated, 100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/2f1b6aa2-e672-4b5f-aeb4-6479ccf56025) (AI windows at High and Medium).

My Brain Feels Damaged's checks, written the same way, read the same: [AI Generated, 100%](https://www.pangram.com/history/0eeefa6e-c72f-4ea6-b74e-fab541aca12f) (AI windows at Medium, High and Low).
suggestions.sense: A fresh reader of my version needed every sentence, "if the pain fades, still let the medics check them" among them, since DMSO can mask pain. The guide's paragraph sets the two kinds against each other ("Mild, familiar, non-progressive discomfort in a fully alert person is different from new, severe, persistent, worsening, radiating, or exertional pain--or pain with breathlessness, sweating, faintness, neurological changes, or collapse") and calls the serious one "the second branch".
suggestions.why: Its shape, two cases, how to tell them apart and what to do when you can't, is one none of your lessons has had yet: you taught when to get help (Risk of Harm), what to find out (Recent Oral Toxic Ingestion) and which signs count (Serotonin Syndrome). Acute Medical and Neurological Rescue's opening (calm the trip where they are, or call) has it too.
suggestions.advice_note: Edit it: say how you'd tell mild chest pain from the serious kind, and what to do with each, in your words. Keep each sign of the serious kind (new, severe, persistent, worsening, spreading, brought on by effort, or with breathlessness, sweating, faintness, neurological changes or collapse), what to do when unsure, and that DMSO can block pain. Your version goes in whole, and I test what it teaches on the sections above.

suggestions.title: 2. Serotonin Syndrome: "the these" fixed, or your exact text?
suggestions.question:
Your version says "One or more of the these patterns makes the diagnosis more likely:". How each option would read:

A (my pick): "One or more of these patterns makes the diagnosis more likely:", as the guide has it now: [Human Written, the heading and first sentence Medium, the rest High](https://www.pangram.com/history/0dfe5d10-9de1-43ad-8062-4dedd8b8fea2). Pro: no doubled word for a reader to trip on. Con: the first sentence reads Medium.

B: your exact text, "the these" kept: [Human Written, High throughout](https://www.pangram.com/history/9e32c090-a4bd-4353-abcc-f56393b6b644). Pro: High everywhere. Con: a reader sees "the these".
suggestions.why: It is your version, and fixing the doubled word lowers its first sentence from High to Medium.
suggestions.advice_note: A, fairly sure: a reader trips on "the these", and a Medium window is fine by your rule (no Low window, most of the text High).
